data.name: Lennart
data.gender_notes: Lennart is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Lennart is of Old Norse origin, derived from the Old Norse elements leynir (hiding place) and herr (ruler or master). It can be interpreted as 'ruler of the hiding place' or 'master of the hiding place'. In Norse mythology, Leynir was a god associated with protection and safety. The name Lennart carries the meaning “Free man” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Lennart usually hope their child will grow to embody free man and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Lennart belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Free man.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lennart total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Lennart may have Scandinavian roots, but it has been embraced by the Christian community. In the Middle Ages, when many personal names were derived from the saints and their virtues, Lennart may have been given to boys to reflect the idea of a protector – someone who hides or shields his charges from harm.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Lennart can be traced back to the Norse god Leynir, as well as to Christian concepts of protection and leadership. For Christians, the name Lennart represents the idea of God as a protector and ruler who is in control of our lives and shields us from the trials and tribulations of the world. It is also a reminder of the spiritual leadership that every Christian is called to exercise in their own lives and in the lives of those around them. Ultimately, the name Lennart inspires us to seek the guidance and protection of God, and to be leaders and protectors in our own right, following the example of Christ.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lennart may be derived from Old Norse elements meaning "ruler of light," emphasizing the triumph of light over darkness, a common Christian theme representing God's power and grace.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Lennart was a 12th century Danish king. The name Lennart carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Lennart continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Ruth Lennart in Rome, Italy credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Lennart, which means "Free man". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
